+    128 devices: sfc 14 rounds, metis 19).  ONE definition, so a scorer that
+    reports which ownership ran cannot drift from what the reorder does.
+    """

+    return resolve_partition_method(method)

Honesty: iter-200 over-attributed a physical effect to numerics. |

Guard test; 11 fall + 331 micro/dycore tests pass (10 `-k`-caught fails pre-existing/unrelated). |
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r6_2026-08-02.md-7974-docs/dev-notes/CRM_faithful_SAM.md-232-| 207-208 | **Cloud-100% reframed (small-domain anvil, NOT a threshold artifact) + bug #6 validation A/B launched.** The compare metric is the PEAK domain cloud fraction (`np.max(cloud)` over levels; RCEMIP 0.08-0.30). legoESM's peak ≈1.0 = the ANVIL covering the WHOLE non-organized 144 km domain — a REAL over-cloud vs RCEMIP, but SMALL-DOMAIN/compute-bound (organized RCE confines the anvil to ~20-30%). **Cloud-threshold audit:** gSAM `statistics.f90:674` uses `coef=min(1e-5, 0.01·qsatw(T,p))` (1e-5 warm trop → ~1e-7 cold anvil); legoESM uses fixed 1e-6 (RCEMIP-protocol, Wing 2018 Tab A2). gSAM unbuildable ⇒ we compare to RCEMIP-PUBLISHED (1e-6 convention) ⇒ 1e-6 is correct, NOT a bug; the cloud-100% peak is anvil-condensate-thick (0.14-0.57 g/kg ≫ both thresholds), robust to either. **Launched `rce_icefall`** = rce_long's CLI with ONLY bug #6's `fall_b_i=0.865` differing — tests whether faster ice fall thins the anvil ⇒ lower peak cloud (A/B vs rce_long b=1.0). Found rce_long's iter-200 kill had FAILED (ran to step 28800; anvil ice declined 0.57→0.14 g/kg as the spin-up settled, cloud stayed 1.0). A/B reads next iter. |
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r6_2026-08-02.md-7975-docs/dev-notes/CRM_faithful_SAM.md:233:| 209-212 | **BUG #7 (ice fall density) + fall-speed/micro audit COMPLETE + A/B + snow 2-mom.** **#7:** ice fall DENSITY exponent 0.54→**0.35** (gSAM `AIN=(RHOSU/RHO)^0.35·AI` Ikawa-Saito, used in `UMI=AIN·CONS28/LAMI^BI`; rain/snow/graupel correctly KEEP 0.54) — was ~25% too fast in thin air; `morrison.py` `dum_i=(ρ_su/ρ)^0.35` for V_t_i+V_n_i. **#6+#7 ⇒ ice fall matches gSAM EXACTLY.** Verified faithful (no more bugs): ALL caps (ice `1.2·(ρsu/ρ)^0.35`, rain `9.1·dum`, snow/graupel `1.2·dum`/`20·dum`), ice deposition (`EPSI=2π·N_i·ρ·DV/LAMI`≡gSAM, `PRD=EPSI·(qv−qsi)/ABI`), LAMI slope (`CONS12=π·ρ_ci`, ρ_ci=500), 2-MOMENT snow (N_s slot 9 ⇒ PSD fall + PRDS/PSACWS/PSMLT/NSAGG — the old "single-moment snow gap" is stale). **rce_icefall A/B (b=0.865 vs rce_long b=1.0):** anvil q_cloud 0.53-0.67 g/kg in BOTH ⇒ the ~3× faster ice fall did NOT cut the cloud-100% — the anvil is DETRAINMENT-dominated + small-domain (fixes are source-faithful, not the cloud-100% cause). 82 micro/dycore tests GREEN ⇒ M2005 microphysics THOROUGHLY faithful. |
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r6_2026-08-02.md-7976-docs/dev-notes/CRM_faithful_SAM.md-234-| 213 | **Closed the documented secondary SGS gap (#8): SAM dosmagor's WEAKLY-stable Deardorff mixing-length limit.** Verified SAM `tke_full.f90:285-298` dosmagor DOES apply, where N²>0: `smix=min(grd, max(0.1·grd, √(0.76·tk/(Ck·√N²))))` + `Cee=Ce1+Ce2·(smix/grd)` ⇒ `tk=√(Ck³/Cee·(|S|²−Pr·N²))·smix²` (Ck=0.1, Ce=Ck³/Cs⁴, Ce1/Ce2=Ce/0.7·{0.19,0.51}). legoESM used the pure `(Cs·Δ)²·|S|` (smix=grd always) ⇒ OVER-mixed in WEAKLY-stable layers (the |S|²−Pr·N² cutoff already matched SAM in unstable + strongly-stable). **FIX:** `smagorinsky_stability_length` (config + `--smag-stability-length`), in BOTH serial + halo K_m (2-pass: smix=grd tk estimate → Deardorff smix, as SAM lags tk; reduces EXACTLY to the pure form where N²≤0). Default False = BYTE-IDENTICAL. Tested (unstable identical, weakly-stable strictly reduces K_m, serial mirrors halo); 8 closure + 24 dycore GREEN. Minor effect (stratosphere/inversion, NOT the convective signal) but closes the LAST characterized SGS gap ⇒ the SGS now FULLY matches SAM dosmagor (with `--smag-stability-length --no-smag-wall-damping`). |

.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r6_2026-08-02.md-8212-./docs/dev-notes/CRM_faithful_SAM.md:233:| 209-212 | **BUG #7 (ice fall density) + fall-speed/micro audit COMPLETE + A/B + snow 2-mom.** **#7:** ice fall DENSITY exponent 0.54→**0.35** (gSAM `AIN=(RHOSU/RHO)^0.35·AI` Ikawa-Saito, used in `UMI=AIN·CONS28/LAMI^BI`; rain/snow/graupel correctly KEEP 0.54) — was ~25% too fast in thin air; `morrison.py` `dum_i=(ρ_su/ρ)^0.35` for V_t_i+V_n_i. **#6+#7 ⇒ ice fall matches gSAM EXACTLY.** Verified faithful (no more bugs): ALL caps (ice `1.2·(ρsu/ρ)^0.35`, rain `9.1·dum`, snow/graupel `1.2·dum`/`20·dum`), ice deposition (`EPSI=2π·N_i·ρ·DV/LAMI`≡gSAM, `PRD=EPSI·(qv−qsi)/ABI`), LAMI slope (`CONS12=π·ρ_ci`, ρ_ci=500), 2-MOMENT snow (N_s slot 9 ⇒ PSD fall + PRDS/PSACWS/PSMLT/NSAGG — the old "single-moment snow gap" is stale). **rce_icefall A/B (b=0.865 vs rce_long b=1.0):** anvil q_cloud 0.53-0.67 g/kg in BOTH ⇒ the ~3× faster ice fall did NOT cut the cloud-100% — the anvil is DETRAINMENT-dominated + small-domain (fixes are source-faithful, not the cloud-100% cause). 82 micro/dycore tests GREEN ⇒ M2005 microphysics THOROUGHLY faithful. |
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r6_2026-08-02.md-8213-./docs/dev-notes/CRM_faithful_SAM.md-234-| 213 | **Closed the documented secondary SGS gap (#8): SAM dosmagor's WEAKLY-stable Deardorff mixing-length limit.** Verified SAM `tke_full.f90:285-298` dosmagor DOES apply, where N²>0: `smix=min(grd, max(0.1·grd, √(0.76·tk/(Ck·√N²))))` + `Cee=Ce1+Ce2·(smix/grd)` ⇒ `tk=√(Ck³/Cee·(|S|²−Pr·N²))·smix²` (Ck=0.1, Ce=Ck³/Cs⁴, Ce1/Ce2=Ce/0.7·{0.19,0.51}). legoESM used the pure `(Cs·Δ)²·|S|` (smix=grd always) ⇒ OVER-mixed in WEAKLY-stable layers (the |S|²−Pr·N² cutoff already matched SAM in unstable + strongly-stable). **FIX:** `smagorinsky_stability_length` (config + `--smag-stability-length`), in BOTH serial + halo K_m (2-pass: smix=grd tk estimate → Deardorff smix, as SAM lags tk; reduces EXACTLY to the pure form where N²≤0). Default False = BYTE-IDENTICAL. Tested (unstable identical, weakly-stable strictly reduces K_m, serial mirrors halo); 8 closure + 24 dycore GREEN. Minor effect (stratosphere/inversion, NOT the convective signal) but closes the LAST characterized SGS gap ⇒ the SGS now FULLY matches SAM dosmagor (with `--smag-stability-length --no-smag-wall-damping`). |

.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-959-12939:1. The METIS matrix does not hold every arm at exactly 5,120 cells/rank. The receipts show geometric 5,120–5,121, but METIS is 5,100–5,145 at 32 ranks and 5,093–5,144 at 128. The wording at [the Phase-3 table](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/.claude/worktrees/scaling-campaign/docs/performance/scaling/levante_campaign_2026-07-24.md:1594) is false; call it a nominal 5,120-cell target and report min/max.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-960-12940-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md:961:12941:2. “Partition-quality lever DEAD/refuted” overclaims. This is evidence that this METIS configuration loses to geometric at L8/128 despite lower cut/halo metrics; it does not eliminate partition quality or mapping generally. The 32→128 terms are weak-scale, 1→4-node scale-out terms, not isolated rank-count terms.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-962-12942-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-963-12943:3. The placement mechanism is misdescribed. Both `block:cyclic` and `block:block` use `block` for rank-to-node placement; the second field changes CPU allocation across sockets. E/D does support “`block:cyclic` is 1.61× faster in this receipt,” but “per-socket bandwidth beats communication locality” is **PLAUSIBLE**, not confirmed.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-964-12944-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-965-12945:4. The METIS receipt ran without parity or conservation gates and logs an unsupported MPI/JAX pairing warning. That does not erase the timing observation, but blocks a production-quality “lever closed” claim until the stack is supported and at least one gated arm per partition passes.

.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_fused_r26_2026-08-04.md-1823-docs/dev-notes/parameterization_checks.md-49-**37. Ocean energy-backscatter OPERATOR (oracle bug 3) — the i47 sign-only audit above ("energy-injection sign correctly ADDED") MISSED the operator ORDER.** Jansen & Held (2014) / Bachman (2019) deterministic backscatter is a NEGATIVE HARMONIC (Laplacian) viscosity `-ν_bs∇²u` (growth ∝ +k²), stabilised by a paired scale-selective biharmonic/Leith dissipation + the `E_max` cap. The code instead returned an ANTI-BIHARMONIC `+∇²(ν_bs∇²u)` (growth ∝ +k⁴) — amplifying the GRID scale MOST (docstring defended it with backwards physics). BOTH forms inject energy (same sign) so the sign-only audit passed; only the spectral character was wrong. **Fixed** (both grids): single (negated) harmonic stress-divergence, coeff `ν_bs=c_bs·Δ·√E` [m²/s] (MPAS Δ³→Δ ⇒ `c_bs` now grid-consistent); injection sign + AD-safety preserved; honest docstring (unstable alone → needs paired biharmonic dissipation; opt-in, NOT yet wired to production). Exact negative-Laplacian regression locks (cgrid+MPAS) falsify the biharmonic two-pass. Codex adversarial review: physics/sign/units/AD/tests all CONFIRMED-CORRECT (1 doc defect found+fixed). **LESSON: a sign-only energy audit cannot certify a backscatter — check the SPECTRAL order (k² vs k⁴).** Screenshot oracle bugs 1,2,4,5,6 (kuo icond2-conservation, edmf flux-form, kpp V_t √βT, harmonic A_h/K_h AD-guard, mle float(ce)) were VERIFIED already-fixed in HEAD (2026-06-29 oracle commits) — that review had run on a pre-fix tree.

.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_fused_r26_2026-08-04.md-1826-.physics-validator/mpas_land_boundary/review-3.md-9-- **CONFIRMED — Medium:** The MPI docstring calls the result “MASS-WEIGHTED” ([model_driver.py:5318](...)), but the implementation/body explicitly uses equal cell weight ([model_driver.py:5332](...), [model_driver.py:6569](...)). True horizontal mass weighting requires `areaCell * dp`; `areaCell` is available on the MPAS grid ([voronoi.py:111](...)). This is a documentation/scientific-label inconsistency, not a vertical-coordinate regression. Block only if the launch’s acceptance claim is an exact mass-weighted global mean.

.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_fused_r26_2026-08-04.md-1927-docs/science/legoesm_documentation.html-39-<h1 id="a0000000004">3 Model Architecture</h1>
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_fused_r26_2026-08-04.md-1928-docs/science/legoesm_documentation.html-40-<p>legoESM is organised as a <em>federation</em> of eight independently installable packages that all ship into one shared <span class="ttfamily">legoesm</span> PEP-420 namespace, layered as an acyclic dependency graph whose import boundaries are enforced by zero-ignore <span class="ttfamily">lint-imports</span> contracts (Fig.&#160;<a href="index.html#fig:dag">1</a>). A single <span class="ttfamily">legoesm-core</span> substrate provides fields, grids, vertical coordinates, operators, the device/precision runtime, the parallel halo/reduction layer, and the grid \(\times \) complexity capability matrix; the four Earth-system components (<span class="ttfamily">atmosphere</span>, <span class="ttfamily">ocean</span>, <span class="ttfamily">land</span>, <span class="ttfamily">ice</span>) depend <em>only</em> on the substrate and never on each other, so each can be <span class="ttfamily">pip install</span>ed and gradient-checked in isolation. Above them sits an orchestration cluster — <span class="ttfamily">coupler</span>+<span class="ttfamily">driver</span>, <span class="ttfamily">ml</span>+<span class="ttfamily">training</span>+<span class="ttfamily">da</span>, and <span class="ttfamily">tools</span> — whose mutual edges form a uv-workspace cycle, so the three install together. </p>

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-61-#     enough to keep cells/device above the threshold answer the question.

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-64-#     ppermute (L6 = 40,962 cells; padded, np8 gives 40,968/8 = 5,121 and
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-65-#     np16 gives 40,976/16 = 2,561 cells/device, each above the 2,000
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-66-#     threshold).  But np8's 7 == n_dev-1 is complete-graph saturation and
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-67-#     says nothing; only np16 (13/10/10 < 15) escapes it.  Still a SMALL
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-68-#     working point; s8-s10 are the production ones.
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-69-#

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-72-#   subdiv-8  sfc 12/14 rounds at 64/128 devices, metis 13/19, geometric 16/21

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-77-#
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch:78:# lloyd=0 throughout: it is what the reference census used AND the cache key

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-80-# synthetic scaling mesh, recorded in every row's metadata so it can never be

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-82-#

.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-959-12939:1. The METIS matrix does not hold every arm at exactly 5,120 cells/rank. The receipts show geometric 5,120–5,121, but METIS is 5,100–5,145 at 32 ranks and 5,093–5,144 at 128. The wording at [the Phase-3 table](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/.claude/worktrees/scaling-campaign/docs/performance/scaling/levante_campaign_2026-07-24.md:1594) is false; call it a nominal 5,120-cell target and report min/max.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-960-12940-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-961-12941:2. “Partition-quality lever DEAD/refuted” overclaims. This is evidence that this METIS configuration loses to geometric at L8/128 despite lower cut/halo metrics; it does not eliminate partition quality or mapping generally. The 32→128 terms are weak-scale, 1→4-node scale-out terms, not isolated rank-count terms.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-962-12942-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-963-12943:3. The placement mechanism is misdescribed. Both `block:cyclic` and `block:block` use `block` for rank-to-node placement; the second field changes CPU allocation across sockets. E/D does support “`block:cyclic` is 1.61× faster in this receipt,” but “per-socket bandwidth beats communication locality” is **PLAUSIBLE**, not confirmed.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-964-12944-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-965-12945:4. The METIS receipt ran without parity or conservation gates and logs an unsupported MPI/JAX pairing warning. That does not erase the timing observation, but blocks a production-quality “lever closed” claim until the stack is supported and at least one gated arm per partition passes.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-966-12946-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md:967:12947:5. The s8→s9 weak-pair claim is confounded. s9 explicitly used `lloyd=0`; the s8 source predates the `--lloyd` option and therefore used the generator’s default production relaxation. They are not the “same protocol.” The first two comparator points are also from the earlier np2–16 ladder, not the claimed np32–128 extension rows. Remove the causal GPU rank-count claim and the plot annotation until s8 is rerun with `lloyd=0` and matched reorder policy.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-968-12948-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-969-12949:6. “Consistent ~1.4×” is arithmetically false: the three costs are 1.80×, 1.35×, and 1.41×. The first is a large outlier. The proposed GPU rank-count term is therefore **PLAUSIBLE at best**, even after the Lloyd confound is fixed.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-970-12950-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-971-12951:7. The reported mesh counts are natural, not executed padded counts. The s9 receipt executed 2,621,568 cells, not 2,621,442; its np32 provenance SHA is also `unknown`. Throughput rounding remains correct, but report executed `n_cells` and resolve that provenance hole. “New MPAS-atmosphere peak” should be scoped to the synthetic, `physics=none` benchmark.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-972-12952-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-973-12953:8. “Floor confirmed” should be **PLAUSIBLE/consistent with the floor**, not CONFIRMED: one below-floor point anti-scales, with no replication and known shape/codegen variation.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-974-12954-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-975-12955:9. The ensemble script masks failures: each background `run_arm` changes `rc` only in its subshell, and `srun ... || { rc=1; }` returns success. Missing/corrupt JSON is silently skipped, so the job can print `DONE rc=0`. [The script](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/.claude/worktrees/scaling-campaign/scripts/tmp/mpas_s9_ensemble.sbatch:44) must preserve each background PID/status and require all five valid receipts. It is also ignored by Git, so it is not reproducibly reviewable.
--

.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-836-#     this undirected graph is exhausted".
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-837-# (c) WHY NOT CHEAPER: this IS the cheap test — no GPU, no MPI, no model
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-838-#     step.  It cannot be shrunk further onto small meshes: measured
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-839-#     2026-08-07, L2/L4 x {geometric,sfc} x nd 2-16 all report gap == 0,
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-840-#     but EVERY one of those rows auto-selects the ALLGATHER strategy
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-841-#     (cells/device below the threshold), so production runs no ppermute
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-842-#     schedule there and the number is counterfactual.  Only meshes big
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-843-#     enough to keep cells/device above the threshold answer the question.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md:844:#     s6 lloyd=0 also gave gap == 0 on all three methods — rounds 7/7/6 at
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-845-#     np8 and 13/10/10 at np16 for geometric/sfc/metis.  Both are genuinely
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-846-#     ppermute (L6 = 40,962 cells; padded, np8 gives 40,968/8 = 5,121 and
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-847-#     np16 gives 40,976/16 = 2,561 cells/device, each above the 2,000
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-848-#     threshold).  But np8's 7 == n_dev-1 is complete-graph saturation and
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-849-#     says nothing; only np16 (13/10/10 < 15) escapes it.  Still a SMALL
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-850-#     working point; s8-s10 are the production ones.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-851-#
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-852-# ARM 1 IS AN INSTRUMENT CHECK, NOT A RESULT.  spmd_schedule_cost's
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md:853:# docstring carries a reference census on the unrelaxed (lloyd=0) mesh:
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md:854:#   subdiv-8  sfc 12/14 rounds at 64/128 devices, metis 13/19, geometric 16/21
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-855-#   subdiv-9  sfc 11/13,                          metis 14/18, geometric 14/18
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-856-# Arms 1-2 must REPRODUCE those before arm 3's unknown s10 number is quoted.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-857-# A scan that misses the known answer is a broken instrument, and its s10
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-858-# row must not be believed.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-859-#
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md:860:# lloyd=0 throughout: it is what the reference census used AND the cache key
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-861-# the prewarmed s8/s9/s10 meshes were written under.  It is the LABELLED
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-862-# synthetic scaling mesh, recorded in every row's metadata so it can never be
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-863-# read back as a production SCVT receipt.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-864-#
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-865-# Arms run cheapest-first and each writes its own JSON, so a later arm that
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-866-# runs out of time or memory cannot lose an earlier arm's result.  s10@128 is
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-867-# last and is the one genuinely at risk: the scorer is known not to have
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_review_schedule_cost_r8_2026-08-07.md-868-# finished at subdiv-8@128 on a laptop, which is why this asks for 24 h.

988-"""Exit-status regression for the MPAS schedule-cost scan launcher.
989-
990:The failure this guards is not hypothetical: the first version of the script
991-captured arm 3's status into ``RC10`` and then ended on a successful ``echo``,
992:so a scan that produced NO valid s10 result exited 0 and SLURM filed it as
993-COMPLETED (codex round 2, BLOCKER).  "Tool status is not evidence" cuts both
994:ways — a launcher that cannot report failure makes every downstream reading
995-of ``sacct`` a lie.
996-
997-HOW THIS IS DRIVEN, and why not the obvious way: the bench path in the
998-launcher is deliberately NOT overridable from the environment.  Making it
999-overridable (the first attempt) handed a stray exported variable the power to
1000-redirect a real scan to something that exits 0 — reintroducing the very
1001:failure class under test (codex round 4).  Instead this substitutes the
1002-INTERPRETER via ``LEGOESM_PYTHON``, which is an existing production knob that
1003-``_env.sh`` already reads, so the launcher itself carries no test-only seam.
1004-
1005-The stub interpreter answers ``_env.sh``'s jax probe, then exits with a
1006-scripted status per arm, recording each arm's full argv so a test can assert
1007-both WHICH arms ran and that each carried its required flags.
1008-"""

2498-    57	#     2026-08-07, L2/L4 x {geometric,sfc} x nd 2-16 all report gap == 0,
2499-    58	#     but EVERY one of those rows auto-selects the ALLGATHER strategy
2500-    59	#     (cells/device below the threshold), so production runs no ppermute
2501-    60	#     schedule there and the number is counterfactual.  Only meshes big
2502-    61	#     enough to keep cells/device above the threshold answer the question.
2503-    62	#     s6 lloyd=0 also gave gap == 0 on all three methods — rounds 7/7/6 at
2504-    63	#     np8 and 13/10/10 at np16 for geometric/sfc/metis.  Both are genuinely
2505-    64	#     ppermute (L6 = 40,962 cells; padded, np8 gives 40,968/8 = 5,121 and
2506-    65	#     np16 gives 40,976/16 = 2,561 cells/device, each above the 2,000
2507-    66	#     threshold).  But np8's 7 == n_dev-1 is complete-graph saturation and
2508-    67	#     says nothing; only np16 (13/10/10 < 15) escapes it.  Still a SMALL
2509-    68	#     working point; s8-s10 are the production ones.
2510-    69	#
2511-    70	# ARM 1 IS AN INSTRUMENT CHECK, NOT A RESULT.  spmd_schedule_cost's
2512:    71	# docstring carries a reference census on the unrelaxed (lloyd=0) mesh:
2513:    72	#   subdiv-8  sfc 12/14 rounds at 64/128 devices, metis 13/19, geometric 16/21
2514:    73	#   subdiv-9  sfc 11/13,                          metis 14/18, geometric 14/18
2515-    74	# Arms 1-2 must REPRODUCE those before arm 3's unknown s10 number is quoted.
2516-    75	# A scan that misses the known answer is a broken instrument, and its s10
2517-    76	# row must not be believed.
2518-    77	#
2519:    78	# lloyd=0 throughout: it is what the reference census used AND the cache key
2520-    79	# the prewarmed s8/s9/s10 meshes were written under.  It is the LABELLED
2521-    80	# synthetic scaling mesh, recorded in every row's metadata so it can never be
2522-    81	# read back as a production SCVT receipt.
2523-    82	#
2524-    83	# Arms run cheapest-first and each writes its own JSON, so a later arm that
2525:    84	# runs out of time or memory cannot lose an earlier arm's result.  s10@128 is
2526-    85	# last and is the one genuinely at risk: the scorer is known not to have
2527-    86	# finished at subdiv-8@128 on a laptop, which is why this asks for 24 h.

2585-   144	  # successful artifact this is supposed to catch (codex round 6).
2586-   145	  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && ! "$PY" -c '

2603-   162	    and "n_rounds" in r["schedule"]
2604-   163	    for r in rows
2605-   164	)
2606-   165	sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

2647-     1	"""Exit-status regression for the MPAS schedule-cost scan launcher.
2648-     2	
2649:     3	The failure this guards is not hypothetical: the first version of the script
2650-     4	captured arm 3's status into ``RC10`` and then ended on a successful ``echo``,
2651:     5	so a scan that produced NO valid s10 result exited 0 and SLURM filed it as
2652-     6	COMPLETED (codex round 2, BLOCKER).  "Tool status is not evidence" cuts both
2653:     7	ways — a launcher that cannot report failure makes every downstream reading
2654-     8	of ``sacct`` a lie.
2655-     9	
2656-    10	HOW THIS IS DRIVEN, and why not the obvious way: the bench path in the
2657-    11	launcher is deliberately NOT overridable from the environment.  Making it
2658-    12	overridable (the first attempt) handed a stray exported variable the power to
2659-    13	redirect a real scan to something that exits 0 — reintroducing the very
2660:    14	failure class under test (codex round 4).  Instead this substitutes the
2661-    15	INTERPRETER via ``LEGOESM_PYTHON``, which is an existing production knob that
2662-    16	``_env.sh`` already reads, so the launcher itself carries no test-only seam.
2663-    17	
2664-    18	The stub interpreter answers ``_env.sh``'s jax probe, then exits with a
2665-    19	scripted status per arm, recording each arm's full argv so a test can assert
2666-    20	both WHICH arms ran and that each carried its required flags.
2667-    21	"""

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-10-# ===========================================================================
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-11-# Does RECOLOURING still have room on the MPAS halo schedule?  CPU-only,
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-12-# ZERO GPU hours.
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-13-#
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-14-# Note this is NOT a two-way choice between colouring and ownership: a
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-15-# redesigned DIRECTED schedule (see the SCOPE note below) is a third path,
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-16-# and it is not bounded by the quantity measured here.  What this run
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-17-# settles is only whether recolouring THIS undirected graph is exhausted.
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-18-#
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-19-# WHY THIS RUN EXISTS
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-20-# MPAS GPU is the worst-scaling lane we have: measured/modelled-bound 3.16x
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch:21:# (s8@16) to 4.47x (s9@64), and one halo fill costs 12-14 SEQUENTIAL ppermute
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-22-# rounds.  Both independent reviews (codex + GLM, 2026-08-07) ranked cutting
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-23-# that round count as the top structural lever, at 300-800 LOC and 7-14 days
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-24-# for a partitioner with a new objective.  That estimate is only worth
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-25-# spending if recolouring is genuinely exhausted, and the colourer's own
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-26-# lower bound decides it.
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-27-#
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-28-# The schedule is a proper EDGE colouring of the device communication graph
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-29-# (one colour = one ppermute round) and max_degree is that graph's maximum
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-30-# vertex degree, so VIZING bounds the chromatic index: Delta <= chi' <=
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-31-# Delta + 1.  Read coloring_gap = n_rounds - max_degree through that:
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-32-#     gap == 0 -> PROVABLY OPTIMAL; recolouring headroom is exactly zero.
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-33-#     gap == 1 -> indistinguishable from optimal (a Class 2 graph really

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-72-#   subdiv-8  sfc 12/14 rounds at 64/128 devices, metis 13/19, geometric 16/21
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-73-#   subdiv-9  sfc 11/13,                          metis 14/18, geometric 14/18
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-74-# Arms 1-2 must REPRODUCE those before arm 3's unknown s10 number is quoted.
scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-75-# A scan that misses the known answer is a broken instrument, and its s10

scripts/cluster/scaling_levante/mpas_schedule_cost_scan.sbatch-77-#

.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-958-12938-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-959-12939:1. The METIS matrix does not hold every arm at exactly 5,120 cells/rank. The receipts show geometric 5,120–5,121, but METIS is 5,100–5,145 at 32 ranks and 5,093–5,144 at 128. The wording at [the Phase-3 table](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/.claude/worktrees/scaling-campaign/docs/performance/scaling/levante_campaign_2026-07-24.md:1594) is false; call it a nominal 5,120-cell target and report min/max.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-960-12940-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-961-12941:2. “Partition-quality lever DEAD/refuted” overclaims. This is evidence that this METIS configuration loses to geometric at L8/128 despite lower cut/halo metrics; it does not eliminate partition quality or mapping generally. The 32→128 terms are weak-scale, 1→4-node scale-out terms, not isolated rank-count terms.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-962-12942-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-963-12943:3. The placement mechanism is misdescribed. Both `block:cyclic` and `block:block` use `block` for rank-to-node placement; the second field changes CPU allocation across sockets. E/D does support “`block:cyclic` is 1.61× faster in this receipt,” but “per-socket bandwidth beats communication locality” is **PLAUSIBLE**, not confirmed.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-964-12944-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-965-12945:4. The METIS receipt ran without parity or conservation gates and logs an unsupported MPI/JAX pairing warning. That does not erase the timing observation, but blocks a production-quality “lever closed” claim until the stack is supported and at least one gated arm per partition passes.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-966-12946-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-967-12947:5. The s8→s9 weak-pair claim is confounded. s9 explicitly used `lloyd=0`; the s8 source predates the `--lloyd` option and therefore used the generator’s default production relaxation. They are not the “same protocol.” The first two comparator points are also from the earlier np2–16 ladder, not the claimed np32–128 extension rows. Remove the causal GPU rank-count claim and the plot annotation until s8 is rerun with `lloyd=0` and matched reorder policy.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-968-12948-
--
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-976-12956-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-977-12957:10. GPU binding is otherwise sound: `--gpu-bind=none` leaves all GPUs visible and JAX’s Slurm auto-detection selects by local rank. Full-GPU `--exact` requests should force disjoint eight-node steps. But log each `SLURM_STEP_NODELIST` and coordinator host; that is the evidence the shared JAX job-ID port is safe.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-978-12958-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-979-12959:11. The ensemble does not synchronize measurement windows, pair each replica topology with a solo control, or counterbalance solo-first ordering. It can measure different node/fabric groups or non-overlapping windows rather than contention. Twelve steps give nine dependent steady samples per launch, not enough independent evidence for a 10% confirmation bar.
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-980-12960-
.physics-validator/scaling_campaign/codex_recovery_review_r2_2026-08-02.md-981-12961:12. Ensemble arithmetic needs tighter wording: if solo reproduces 5.47 GC/s, ideal aggregate is 21.88 GC/s. The 1.10 threshold guarantees only 19.89 GC/s = 3.636× the 32-GPU solo rate, or 3.35× the observed 128-GPU single trajectory—not 21.9 GC/s.

   100	                          moist=False, lloyd_iterations=50):
   101	    """Reordered+padded global mesh, MPAS PE model, baroclinic-wave IC.
   102	
   103	    ``reorder_target`` sets the PARTITION (and ghost padding) so every run
   104	    of a strong-scaling ladder times the IDENTICAL mesh; ``run_nd`` is the
   105	    device count of THIS run's mesh/model (the two differ for the
   106	    single-device reference leg of a ladder, via ``--reorder-for``).
   107	    ``moist=True`` attaches the q_v/q_c/q_r tracers (moist baroclinic
   108	    wave) so the sharded step's packed tracer halo exchange + RK tracer
   109	    advection sit on the timed/gated path.
   110	    """

   123	    if run_nd > 1 and (mesh.nCells % run_nd or mesh.nEdges % run_nd):

scripts/bench/roofline_probe.py-86-DRAM traffic beyond the single-pass read is of order the halo ring plus

scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-7-
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-8-* **payload-bound** — the time is real bytes on the wire.  Cutting the ROUND
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-9-  COUNT then saves only the per-round latency (~30 us x rounds removed), not
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-10-  the transfer, because the same bytes still have to move.  That is the LOW
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-11-  end of a round-depth partitioner's value.
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-12-* **wait-bound** — the collective blocks until the slowest peer arrives, so
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-13-  the duration is mostly idle.  Cutting rounds then saves much more, but so
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-14-  would fixing the imbalance, and a partitioner that ignores it may buy
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-15-  nothing.

scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-17-This script separates them from an EXISTING trace, with no GPU job:
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-18-
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-19-1. **Reproducibility.** Group the ``SendRecv`` durations by position in the
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-20-   repeating schedule (period auto-detected by minimising within-position
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-21-   variation).  Random rank jitter cannot reproduce; a structural per-round
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-22-   cost can.  Report within-position CV against the overall CV.
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-23-2. **Payload correlation.** Pair each position with the payload the

scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-25-   round_profile_for_device=)``) and correlate.  High correlation =>
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-26-   payload-bound.  Near-zero => the duration is not explained by what is
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-27-   being sent, i.e. wait.
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-28-
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-29-Correlation is used deliberately because it is SCALE-FREE in the absolute
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-30-sense: no assumption about bytes-per-value, bandwidth or field count can move

scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-32-every assumption — the exchange sends ``cells * cell_width + edges * nlev``
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-33-values, so the RATIO of those two widths re-weights the payload and could in
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-34-principle move the correlation.  The report therefore also gives the
scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py-35-cells-only correlation as a sensitivity; if the two agree, the verdict does

+def _round_profile(sched, device, n_dev):
+    """Per-round payload for ONE device, in the order it observes them.
+
+    See ``spmd_schedule_cost``'s ``round_profile_for_device``.  Only rounds
+    whose colour class touches *device* are returned, because those are the
+    only ones on which it issues a collective.
+    """
+    if not 0 <= int(device) < n_dev:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"round_profile_for_device must be in [0, {n_dev}), got {device!r}")
+    device = int(device)
+    out = []
+    for r, perm in enumerate(sched["ppermute_perms"]):
+        partner = next((dst for src, dst in perm if src == device), None)
+        if partner is None:
+            continue

+        # right payload measure rather than a per-pair count: the index
+        # arrays are (n_dev, max_c) and ppermute moves the padded buffer, so
+        # every pair in the round puts max_c entities on the wire.  (The
+        # per-pair send maps cannot be recovered from those arrays anyway --
+        # they are zero-padded and 0 is a valid index.)
+        out.append({
+            "round": r,
+            "partner": int(partner),
+            "halo_cells": int(sched["halo_cells_per_round"][r]),
+            "halo_edges": int(sched["halo_edges_per_round"][r]),
+        })

     4	The MPAS GPU lane spends most of its step inside ``ncclDevKernel_SendRecv``
     5	(s9/np64: 5.94 of 9.72 ms on rank 0), at a median far above the clean wire
     6	estimate.  Two mechanisms explain that, and they imply OPPOSITE engineering:
     7	
     8	* **payload-bound** — the time is real bytes on the wire.  Cutting the ROUND
     9	  COUNT then saves only the per-round latency (~30 us x rounds removed), not
    10	  the transfer, because the same bytes still have to move.  That is the LOW
    11	  end of a round-depth partitioner's value.
    12	* **wait-bound** — the collective blocks until the slowest peer arrives, so
    13	  the duration is mostly idle.  Cutting rounds then saves much more, but so
    14	  would fixing the imbalance, and a partitioner that ignores it may buy
    15	  nothing.
    16	
    17	This script separates them from an EXISTING trace, with no GPU job:
    18	
    19	1. **Reproducibility.** Group the ``SendRecv`` durations by position in the
    20	   repeating schedule (period auto-detected by minimising within-position
    21	   variation).  Random rank jitter cannot reproduce; a structural per-round
    22	   cost can.  Report within-position CV against the overall CV.
    23	2. **Payload correlation.** Pair each position with the payload the
    24	   production schedule says that round moves (``spmd_schedule_cost(...,
    25	   round_profile_for_device=)``) and correlate.  High correlation =>
    26	   payload-bound.  Near-zero => the duration is not explained by what is
    27	   being sent, i.e. wait.
    28	
    29	Correlation is used deliberately because it is SCALE-FREE in the absolute
    30	sense: no assumption about bytes-per-value, bandwidth or field count can move
    31	it, and those are the assumptions most likely to be wrong.  It is NOT free of
    32	every assumption — the exchange sends ``cells * cell_width + edges * nlev``
    33	values, so the RATIO of those two widths re-weights the payload and could in
    34	principle move the correlation.  The report therefore also gives the
    35	cells-only correlation as a sensitivity; if the two agree, the verdict does
    36	not rest on ``--cell-pack-width``.

    38	ALIGNMENT, the thing that silently corrupts this comparison: an nsys capture
    39	is per RANK, and a rank issues a collective only in the colour classes that
    40	touch it.  At s9/np64 rank 0 shows 8 ``SendRecv`` per halo fill while the
    41	graph's ``max_degree`` is 11.  So the k-th observed call is the k-th round

    44	detected period divides the trace length; when it does not, the schedule and

    76	def sendrecv_durations_us(sqlite_path: str, kernel_like: str = _SENDRECV_LIKE):

    94	def _within_cv(durations, period, min_cycles):

   103	def detect_period(durations, device_rounds, min_cycles: int = 3,
   104	                  max_fills: int = 8, tolerance: float = 1.25):
   105	    """Schedule period, chosen among STRUCTURALLY POSSIBLE candidates only.
   106	
   107	    Returns ``(period, within_cv, overall_cv, candidates)``.
   108	
   109	    A free scan over every period is INVALID here, and the first version of
   110	    this script was: within-position CV falls mechanically as the period
   111	    grows, because each position then holds fewer samples.  Scanning 2..64
   112	    over a 288-call trace duly picked 64 -- the largest allowed -- and would
   113	    have picked whatever ceiling it was given.
   114	
   115	    The schedule constrains it instead.  One halo fill costs the device
   116	    ``device_rounds`` collectives, and a step is a whole number of fills, so
   117	    the period must be ``device_rounds * k``.  Among those few candidates,
   118	    take the SMALLEST whose within-position CV is within *tolerance* of the
   119	    best: a larger multiple always fits at least as well (k and 2k induce
   120	    nested groupings), so preferring the smallest is what keeps the answer
   121	    from inflating.
   122	    """
   123	    overall = st.pstdev(durations) / st.mean(durations)
   124	    candidates = []
   125	    for k in range(1, max_fills + 1):
   126	        period = device_rounds * k
   127	        if len(durations) // period < min_cycles:
   128	            break
   129	        cv = _within_cv(durations, period, min_cycles)
   130	        if cv is not None:
   131	            candidates.append({"fills": k, "period": period,
   132	                               "within_cv": round(cv, 4)})
   133	    if not candidates:
   134	        raise SystemExit(
   135	            f"cannot detect a period: {len(durations)} calls is under "
   136	            f"{min_cycles} cycles of even one fill ({device_rounds} rounds). "
   137	            f"Capture more steps.")
   138	    best_cv = min(c["within_cv"] for c in candidates)
   139	    chosen = next(c for c in candidates
   140	                  if c["within_cv"] <= best_cv * tolerance)
   141	    return chosen["period"], chosen["within_cv"], overall, candidates

   144	def pearson(xs, ys):
   145	    n = len(xs)
   146	    if n < 3:
   147	        return None
   148	    mx, my = st.mean(xs), st.mean(ys)
   149	    sx, sy = st.pstdev(xs), st.pstdev(ys)
   150	    if sx == 0 or sy == 0:
   151	        # A constant series has no correlation to report; saying 0.0 would
   152	        # read as "payload does not explain it" when the truth is "payload
   153	        # does not vary here, so this trace cannot answer the question".
   154	        return None
   155	    return sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)) / (n * sx * sy)

   166	    send count does not set its cost.

   169	    edge field over levels), so ``halo_cells + halo_edges`` is NOT the
   170	    payload and correlating against it mis-weights the mixture.
   171	    """
   172	    return halo_cells * cell_width + halo_edges * nlev

@@ -0,0 +1,379 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python
+"""Is a halo collective's time PAYLOAD or WAIT? Decide it from an nsys trace.
+
+The MPAS GPU lane spends most of its step inside ``ncclDevKernel_SendRecv``
+(s9/np64: 5.94 of 9.72 ms on rank 0), at a median far above the clean wire
+estimate.  Two mechanisms explain that, and they imply OPPOSITE engineering:
+
+* **payload-bound** — the time is real bytes on the wire.  Cutting the ROUND
+  COUNT then saves only the per-round latency (~30 us x rounds removed), not
+  the transfer, because the same bytes still have to move.  That is the LOW
+  end of a round-depth partitioner's value.
+* **wait-bound** — the collective blocks until the slowest peer arrives, so
+  the duration is mostly idle.  Cutting rounds then saves much more, but so
+  would fixing the imbalance, and a partitioner that ignores it may buy
+  nothing.
+
+This script separates them from an EXISTING trace, with no GPU job:
+
+1. **Reproducibility.** Group the ``SendRecv`` durations by position in the
+   repeating schedule (period auto-detected by minimising within-position
+   variation).  Random rank jitter cannot reproduce; a structural per-round
+   cost can.  Report within-position CV against the overall CV.
+2. **Payload correlation.** Pair each position with the payload the
+   production schedule says that round moves (``spmd_schedule_cost(...,
+   round_profile_for_device=)``) and correlate.  High correlation =>
+   payload-bound.  Near-zero => the duration is not explained by what is
+   being sent, i.e. wait.
+
+Correlation is used deliberately because it is SCALE-FREE in the absolute
+sense: no assumption about bytes-per-value, bandwidth or field count can move
+it, and those are the assumptions most likely to be wrong.  It is NOT free of
+every assumption — the exchange sends ``cells * cell_width + edges * nlev``
+values, so the RATIO of those two widths re-weights the payload and could in
+principle move the correlation.  The report therefore also gives the
+cells-only correlation as a sensitivity; if the two agree, the verdict does
+not rest on ``--cell-pack-width``.
+
+ALIGNMENT, the thing that silently corrupts this comparison: an nsys capture
+is per RANK, and a rank issues a collective only in the colour classes that
+touch it.  At s9/np64 rank 0 shows 8 ``SendRecv`` per halo fill while the
+graph's ``max_degree`` is 11.  So the k-th observed call is the k-th round
+CONTAINING THAT DEVICE.  ``round_profile_for_device`` returns exactly that
+subset, in order.  The check that this is the RIGHT subset is that the
+detected period divides the trace length; when it does not, the schedule and
+the trace describe different runs and the script REFUSES rather than pairing
+rounds with unrelated collectives.
+
+Run (no GPU needed; the mesh build dominates at subdiv>=9):
+  python scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py \\
+      --sqlite /scratch/.../s9np64_rank0.sqlite \\
+      --subdivision 9 --n-devices 64 --partition-method sfc --lloyd 0 \\
+      --out results/a1/nsys_halo_rounds_s9np64.json
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import sqlite3
+import statistics as st
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
+
+from metadata import scaling_metadata  # noqa: E402
+
+# Measured Levante fabric constants (campaign jobs 26677438/39): IB latency
+# is flat with communicator size but bandwidth HALVES past 2 nodes.
+_IB_LATENCY_US = 29.7
+_IB_BANDWIDTH_GBS = 12.1
+
+_SENDRECV_LIKE = "ncclDevKernel_SendRecv%"
+
+
+def sendrecv_durations_us(sqlite_path: str, kernel_like: str = _SENDRECV_LIKE):
+    """Durations (us) of every matching collective kernel, in launch order."""
+    con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{sqlite_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
+    try:
+        rows = con.execute(
+            "SELECT k.start, k.end FROM CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_KERNEL k "
+            "JOIN StringIds s ON k.demangledName = s.id "
+            "WHERE s.value LIKE ? ORDER BY k.start", (kernel_like,)).fetchall()
+    finally:
+        con.close()
+    if not rows:
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"{sqlite_path}: no kernel matching {kernel_like!r}. Wrong trace, "
+            f"or nsys captured no CUDA kernels — either way there is nothing "
+            f"to measure.")
+    return [(e - s) / 1e3 for s, e in rows]
+
+
+def _within_cv(durations, period, min_cycles):
+    cvs = []
+    for pos in range(period):
+        group = durations[pos::period]
+        if len(group) >= min_cycles and st.mean(group) > 0:
+            cvs.append(st.pstdev(group) / st.mean(group))
+    return st.mean(cvs) if cvs else None
+
+
+def detect_period(durations, device_rounds, min_cycles: int = 3,
+                  max_fills: int = 8, tolerance: float = 1.25):
+    """Schedule period, chosen among STRUCTURALLY POSSIBLE candidates only.
+
+    Returns ``(period, within_cv, overall_cv, candidates)``.
+
+    A free scan over every period is INVALID here, and the first version of
+    this script was: within-position CV falls mechanically as the period
+    grows, because each position then holds fewer samples.  Scanning 2..64
+    over a 288-call trace duly picked 64 -- the largest allowed -- and would
+    have picked whatever ceiling it was given.
+
+    The schedule constrains it instead.  One halo fill costs the device
+    ``device_rounds`` collectives, and a step is a whole number of fills, so
+    the period must be ``device_rounds * k``.  Among those few candidates,
+    take the SMALLEST whose within-position CV is within *tolerance* of the
+    best: a larger multiple always fits at least as well (k and 2k induce
+    nested groupings), so preferring the smallest is what keeps the answer
+    from inflating.
+    """
+    overall = st.pstdev(durations) / st.mean(durations)
+    candidates = []
+    for k in range(1, max_fills + 1):
+        period = device_rounds * k
+        if len(durations) // period < min_cycles:
+            break
+        cv = _within_cv(durations, period, min_cycles)
+        if cv is not None:
+            candidates.append({"fills": k, "period": period,
+                               "within_cv": round(cv, 4)})
+    if not candidates:
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"cannot detect a period: {len(durations)} calls is under "
+            f"{min_cycles} cycles of even one fill ({device_rounds} rounds). "
+            f"Capture more steps.")
+    best_cv = min(c["within_cv"] for c in candidates)
+    chosen = next(c for c in candidates
+                  if c["within_cv"] <= best_cv * tolerance)
+    return chosen["period"], chosen["within_cv"], overall, candidates
+
+
+def pearson(xs, ys):
+    n = len(xs)
+    if n < 3:
+        return None
+    mx, my = st.mean(xs), st.mean(ys)
+    sx, sy = st.pstdev(xs), st.pstdev(ys)
+    if sx == 0 or sy == 0:
+        # A constant series has no correlation to report; saying 0.0 would
+        # read as "payload does not explain it" when the truth is "payload
+        # does not vary here, so this trace cannot answer the question".
+        return None
+    return sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys)) / (n * sx * sy)
+
+
+def payload_values(halo_cells, halo_edges, cell_width, nlev):
+    """Values one device puts on the wire for a round.
+
+    Read off the production exchange (``_ppermute_halo_fill``): it sends
+    ``concatenate(cell_pack[sc].ravel(), u_shard[se].ravel())``, i.e.
+    ``halo_cells * cell_width + halo_edges * nlev`` values, where the row
+    counts are the round's PADDED extents -- the schedule pads every pair to
+    the round maximum and ppermute moves that whole buffer, so a pair's own
+    send count does not set its cost.
+
+    The two terms carry DIFFERENT widths (the packed cell record vs one
+    edge field over levels), so ``halo_cells + halo_edges`` is NOT the
+    payload and correlating against it mis-weights the mixture.
+    """
+    return halo_cells * cell_width + halo_edges * nlev
+
+
+def modeled_us(values, bytes_per_value, latency_us, bandwidth_gbs):
+    """Latency + bytes/bandwidth for one round, as a REFERENCE not a truth."""
+    return latency_us + (values * bytes_per_value) / (bandwidth_gbs * 1e9) * 1e6
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description=__doc__,
+        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    p.add_argument("--sqlite", required=True, help="nsys-exported .sqlite")
+    p.add_argument("--subdivision", type=int, required=True)
+    p.add_argument("--n-devices", type=int, required=True)
+    p.add_argument("--partition-method", default="sfc")
+    p.add_argument("--lloyd", type=int, default=0,
+                   help="Must match the mesh the traced run used.")
+    p.add_argument("--device", type=int, default=0,
+                   help="Rank whose trace this is (default 0).")
+    p.add_argument("--nlev", type=int, default=26)
+    p.add_argument("--cell-pack-width", type=int, default=None,
+                   help="Width W of the packed CELL record the exchange "
+                        "sends (cell_pack is (cells, W)); edges send nlev. "
+                        "Default nlev. Only the RATIO W/nlev affects the "
+                        "correlation, since it re-weights the two payload "
+                        "terms; the report also gives the cells-only "
+                        "correlation as a sensitivity on this assumption.")
+    p.add_argument("--bytes-per-value", type=int, default=4)
+    p.add_argument("--comm-latency-us", type=float, default=_IB_LATENCY_US)
+    p.add_argument("--comm-bandwidth-gbs", type=float,
+                   default=_IB_BANDWIDTH_GBS)
+    p.add_argument("--drop-first-cycles", type=int, default=3,
+                   help="Cycles to discard as warmup/compile.")
+    p.add_argument("--kernel-like", default=_SENDRECV_LIKE)
+    p.add_argument("--out", default="results/a1/nsys_halo_rounds.json")
+    args = p.parse_args()
+
+    if args.lloyd < 0:
+        raise SystemExit(f"--lloyd must be >= 0, got {args.lloyd}")
+    if args.subdivision < 0:
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"--subdivision must be >= 0, got {args.subdivision}")
+
+    cell_width = args.nlev if args.cell_pack_width is None \
+        else args.cell_pack_width
+    durations = sendrecv_durations_us(args.sqlite, args.kernel_like)
+    print(f"[trace] {len(durations)} collectives in {args.sqlite}", flush=True)
+
+    # The SCHEDULE must be built first: it supplies the only structurally
+    # valid period candidates (see detect_period).
+    from legoesm.grids.voronoi import create_voronoi_mesh
+    from legoesm.parallel.sharded_dynamics import spmd_schedule_cost
+
+    print(f"[mesh] building L{args.subdivision} lloyd={args.lloyd} …",
+          flush=True)
+    mesh = create_voronoi_mesh(subdivision_level=args.subdivision,
+                               lloyd_iterations=args.lloyd)
+    cost = spmd_schedule_cost(mesh, args.n_devices,
+                              method=args.partition_method,
+                              round_profile_for_device=args.device)
+    profile = cost["round_profile"]
+    print(f"[sched] n_rounds={cost['n_rounds']} "
+          f"max_degree={cost['max_degree']} "
+          f"device {args.device} participates in {len(profile)}", flush=True)
+    if not profile:
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"device {args.device} participates in no round; nothing to pair.")
+
+    period, within_cv, overall_cv, candidates = detect_period(
+        durations, len(profile))
+    fills_per_cycle = period // len(profile)
+    print(f"[align] period={period} = {len(profile)} rounds x "
+          f"{fills_per_cycle} fill(s); within-position CV {within_cv:.3f} "
+          f"vs overall {overall_cv:.3f}", flush=True)
+    print(f"[align] candidates: {candidates}", flush=True)
+    # THE REAL CONSISTENCY CHECK. An earlier version guarded on
+    # `period % len(profile) == 0`, which is VACUOUS: the period is
+    # constructed as len(profile) * k, so it can never fail. The check with
+    # teeth is that the trace length is a whole number of periods -- the
+    # capture covers complete steps, so if the schedule's round count
+    # described this run, its period would divide the call count.
+    #
+    # This is what caught the s9/np64 case: the trace holds 288 calls (12
+    # steps x 24), but the schedule scored here gives device 0 seven rounds,
+    # and no multiple of 7 divides 288. Reporting a correlation from that
+    # pairing would have been a confident wrong answer (it read r = +0.155,
+    # i.e. "not payload-bound") built on rounds paired with unrelated
+    # collectives.
+    if len(durations) % period:
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"REFUSING to pair: the trace has {len(durations)} collectives, "
+            f"which is not a whole number of periods of {period} "
+            f"({len(durations) / period:.2f}). The schedule scored here "
+            f"(device {args.device} in {len(profile)} of {cost['n_rounds']} "
+            f"rounds) does not describe the traced run.\n"
+            f"Reconcile them before trusting any number: check --subdivision, "
+            f"--n-devices, --partition-method and --lloyd against the run's "
+            f"own manifest, and check whether that run passed a "
+            f"--reorder-for different from its device count (the scorer takes "
+            f"reorder_target for exactly that case).")
+
+    steady = durations[period * args.drop_first_cycles:]
+    if len(steady) < period * 2:
+        raise SystemExit(
+            f"only {len(steady)} calls after dropping "
+            f"{args.drop_first_cycles} cycles of {period}; capture more steps "
+            f"or lower --drop-first-cycles.")
+
+    slots = []
+    for pos in range(period):
+        group = steady[pos::period]
+        entry = profile[pos % len(profile)]
+        med = st.median(group)
+        slots.append({
+            "position": pos,
+            "fill": pos // len(profile),
+            "round": entry["round"],
+            "partner": entry["partner"],
+            "halo_cells": entry["halo_cells"],
+            "halo_edges": entry["halo_edges"],
+            "n": len(group),
+            "median_us": round(med, 2),
+            "cv": round(st.pstdev(group) / st.mean(group), 4),
+            "payload_values": payload_values(
+                entry["halo_cells"], entry["halo_edges"], cell_width,
+                args.nlev),
+            "modeled_us": round(modeled_us(
+                payload_values(entry["halo_cells"], entry["halo_edges"],
+                               cell_width, args.nlev),
+                args.bytes_per_value, args.comm_latency_us,
+                args.comm_bandwidth_gbs), 2),
+        })
+
+    payload = [s["payload_values"] for s in slots]
+    measured = [s["median_us"] for s in slots]
+    r = pearson(payload, measured)
+    # Sensitivity on the one assumption in the payload model (the cell/edge
+    # width ratio): if the cells-only correlation agrees, the verdict does
+    # not hinge on --cell-pack-width.
+    r_cells = pearson([s["halo_cells"] for s in slots], measured)
+    stable = [s for s in slots if s["cv"] <= 0.05]
+
+    print()
+    print(f"{'pos':>3} {'fill':>4} {'rnd':>4} {'partner':>7} {'cells':>8} "
+          f"{'edges':>8} {'values':>10} {'median_us':>10} {'cv':>7} "
+          f"{'model_us':>9}")
+    for s in slots:
+        print(f"{s['position']:3d} {s['fill']:4d} {s['round']:4d} "
+              f"{s['partner']:7d} {s['halo_cells']:8d} {s['halo_edges']:8d} "
+              f"{s['payload_values']:10d} {s['median_us']:10.1f} "
+              f"{s['cv']:7.3f} {s['modeled_us']:9.1f}")
+
+    print()
+    print(f"[reproducibility] {len(stable)}/{len(slots)} positions have "
+          f"CV <= 0.05; overall CV across all calls is {overall_cv:.3f}")
+    print(f"[payload correlation] pearson r = "
+          f"{'n/a' if r is None else f'{r:+.3f}'}"
+          f"{'' if r is None else f'  (r^2 = {r * r:.3f})'}"
+          f"   [cells-only sensitivity r = "
+          f"{'n/a' if r_cells is None else f'{r_cells:+.3f}'}]")
+    print(f"[totals] one cycle of medians = {sum(measured) / 1e3:.3f} ms")
+
+    out = {
+        "slots": slots,
+        "period": period,
+        "fills_per_cycle": fills_per_cycle,
+        "period_candidates": candidates,
+        "within_position_cv": round(within_cv, 4),
+        "overall_cv": round(overall_cv, 4),
+        "payload_correlation_r": None if r is None else round(r, 4),
+        "payload_correlation_r_cells_only": (
+            None if r_cells is None else round(r_cells, 4)),
+        "cell_pack_width": cell_width,
+        "positions_stable_cv_le_0p05": len(stable),
+        "cycle_total_median_ms": round(sum(measured) / 1e3, 4),
+        "n_rounds": cost["n_rounds"],
+        "max_degree": cost["max_degree"],
+        "device_rounds": len(profile),
+        "sqlite": os.path.abspath(args.sqlite),
+        # No verdict string: the interpretation belongs in the analysis after
+        # the controls pass, not baked into the tool where it gets echoed
+        # back as evidence.
+        "metadata": scaling_metadata(
+            grid="voronoi", component="atmosphere",
+            resolution=f"L{args.subdivision}", n_levels=args.nlev,
+            precision="n/a", decomposition="cell_partition",
+            solver_variant="n/a", scaling_kind="halo-round-attribution",
+            transport="nccl",
+            extra={"n_devices": args.n_devices,
+                   "partition_method": args.partition_method,
+                   "lloyd_iterations": args.lloyd,
+                   "device": args.device,
+                   "cell_pack_width_assumed": cell_width,
+                   "comm_latency_us": args.comm_latency_us,
+                   "comm_bandwidth_gbs": args.comm_bandwidth_gbs}),
+    }
+    outdir = os.path.dirname(args.out)
+    if outdir:
+        os.makedirs(outdir, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(args.out, "w") as f:
+        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
+    print(f"JSON: {args.out}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

The tool cannot yet distinguish payload from wait, and its current s9@64 invocation builds the wrong schedule for the traced ownership.

- Payload proxy: the padded round maxima are correct. The schedule takes the max directed cell/edge send count in each colour, makes `(n_dev, max_c/max_e)` rows, and runtime gathers, flattens, concatenates, and permutes the full padded rows—there is no per-pair slice. [schedule construction](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:1967), [runtime exchange](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:2153).  
  But exact payload is `max_c * W + max_e * nlev`, where `W = nlev*(1+n_tracers)+2`, not the current default `W=nlev`. Temperature, `p_s`, `phis`, and tracers are packed together. [pack layout](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:2104), [default](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:216). `--cell-pack-width` must be required from the run manifest or derived from tracer count; cells-only sensitivity does not establish that every plausible `W` gives the same result.

- Alignment: the source loop executes a `ppermute` for every schedule colour; it contains no “if this rank has a partner” branch. [loop](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:2153). The observed eight `SendRecv` kernels may mean XLA emits no NCCL work for unmatched ranks, but that is a lowering fact, not proved by Python source. Confirm it with the dumped GPU HLO/trace for one fill before treating the subset mapping as established.

  More immediately, the analyzer calls `spmd_schedule_cost(..., n_devices=64)` without `reorder_target`. [call](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:230). Production first reorders for `--reorder-for`, then builds the 64-device schedule. [production reorder](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/bench_mpas_spmd_scaling.py:120), [CLI resolution](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/bench_mpas_spmd_scaling.py:308). The scorer explicitly supports this case. [scorer](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:1366). The script’s own `288` vs seven-round observation is therefore evidence of this mismatch, not a reason to stop at refusal. Add and record `--reorder-target`; the cited s9@64 ladder needs `128`.

- The new divisibility refusal is necessary but not a validation of alignment. The detector constructs every candidate as `device_rounds*k`, then only asks whether the trace length divides the selected candidate. [construction](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:115), [check](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:261). An unrelated 288-event trace with an eight-event candidate passes. It also does not establish starting phase. Use explicit step/NVTX boundaries and the known fills-per-step, then reject partial first/last fills.

- Period detection remains biased. Restricting candidates is an improvement, but smaller groups still make the population-CV estimate less stable and downward biased; candidates such as `2k` and `3k` are not nested. The statement that a larger multiple “always fits at least as well” is false, and `1.25` has no statistical interpretation. [selection](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:103). The 195 ms event can also choose the period before any warmup is removed. Supply the known stage/fill cadence; do not infer it from the same samples used for attribution.

- Low within-position CV does not eliminate wait. A consistently late peer, repeatable stream serialization, or a topology-specific path produces stable position-dependent wait. Conversely a high payload correlation is associative, not causal: payload and the identity/workload of the slow peer are both schedule-position covariates. Thus “high r ⇒ payload” and “near-zero r ⇒ wait” are not supported by this trace alone. [claimed inference](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:19). The discriminator needs an A/B that changes packed width/precision or tracer count while holding the schedule fixed, plus cross-rank launch/completion timing to measure arrival skew.

- Trace mining is unsafe for a causal claim. The SQL selects every matching kernel by name and orders only by start time. [query](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:76). It neither verifies one CUDA stream/context nor ties a kernel to this communicator. Excluding the `AllGather_RING_LL` is right for ppermute payload attribution, but proves neither that all remaining `SendRecv` kernels belong to this halo nor that start-time order is source-round order. Export `rowid`, device/context/stream, and correlation IDs; audit duplicate kernel rows; select a marked steady step range. Do not use a fixed prefix drop as a compile/warmup proof. [drop](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:274).

- `pearson(...)=None` for a constant series is correct. [implementation](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:144). But the helper silently reports a numeric answer for unequal lengths (`[1,2,3]` versus `[1,2]` returned `0.408...` in review), because it uses `len(xs)` but `zip`. Add equal-length and finite-value checks. The main path presently builds equal lists, so this is a hardening defect rather than the central false conclusion.

- `--n-fields` is gone in the current tree. The analogous claim is now false: `--cell-pack-width` changes the payload passed to Pearson. [payload/r](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/scripts/bench/analyze_nsys_halo_rounds.py:296). It is only the displayed bandwidth model that is reference-only.

- `_round_profile` has two defects. Its documentation promises `send_cells`/`send_edges`, but returns neither. [promise](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:1327), [return](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:1451). More seriously, `round_profile_for_device=0.9` silently profiles device 0 because validation coerces with `int()`. [validation](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:1436). Match the strict `n_dev` validation.

On the census: colouring non-determinism is ruled out by the code: edges are sorted and shuffles use fixed seeds. [determinism](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:1768), [ordering](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/parallel/sharded_dynamics.py:1790). The new helper also cannot change `n_rounds`; it only reads `sched`.

For the trace mismatch, a different reorder target is a confirmed likely cause. For the entire census mismatch, especially geometric@128 `19` versus `21`, do not guess a single cause: 128 has the same target under either convention. It is either a stale census or a different raw/cached mesh. The discriminating record is: hash the raw mesh connectivity and coordinates, hash the reordered mesh for each `(method, reorder_target)`, and record `max_degree`, `n_rounds_greedy`, colouring method, plus hashes of `comm_pairs` and the final colour map. Cache-on/off and a second process must produce identical hashes; then compare target `64` versus `128` at the 64-device rung. The mesh cache is input-bearing. [cache load](/work/bd1083/b309178/diffESM/legoesm_pg/legoESM/packages/core/legoesm/grids/voronoi.py:1304).
